To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the C-terminal domain is necessary and sufficient for the splicing activation function of RBFOX1, whereas both the RRM and the C-terminal domain are required for the splicing repression function; (ii) hnRNP H and TFG interact with RBFOX1 and modulate its activity.
RBFOX1 and 2 activate or repress splicing in a position-dependent way, and that the C-terminal domain is required for exon repression, but not exon activation.

the position-dependent effects of RBFOX1-2 on alternative splicing are mediated by distinct domains of the protein and are modulated by specific RNA-binding proteins that interact with the C-terminus of RBFOX1, 2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular basis of alternative splicing regulation.
understanding how alternative splicing factors regulate alternative splicing.
the mechanisms of activation and repression of alternative splicing by RBFOX1/ 2.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
RBFOX1/ 2 activate alternative splicing by binding to the 3' splice site of the downstream intron.
hnRNP-H1 modulates the splicing activity and the splicing activity is modulated by hnRNP-H. Mechanisms of Activation and Repression
hnRNP-H1 is a splicing factor that modulates the splicing activity and specificity of the splicing factors RBFOX1 and 2.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

hnRNP-H1 is an essential factor for RBFOX1/1 splicing activation and RRM is essential for RBFOX1 splicing repression, and that the C-terminal domain is required to interact with other proteins to modulate RBFOX1/12 splicing activity.

the C-terminal domain is required for exon activation and interacts with hnRNP H and RALY to mediate exon repression, whereas the RRM is required for exon repression and interacts with hnRNPs A1 and A2B1.
RBFOX splicing activity is modulated by the C-terminal domain in a context-dependent manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the position-dependent activity of splicing factors can be explained by their ability to bind RNA and protein targets.

the position of the splicing factors on the pre-mRNA determines whether they act to repress or activate splicing, and that this is due to differences in the interactions of these factors with the pre-mRNA and other RNA-binding proteins.

the position dependence of RBFOX1 splicing activation and inhibition can be recapitulated using an MS2 tethering assay, and that hnRNP-H1 and RALY may be important for modulating RBFOX1 and/or RBFOX2 activity in cells.
